 11/18 Game Preview: Celtics at Nuggets
 November 18, 2026 11:42 AM EST Provided by Field Level Media 
 The Boston Celtics suffered what can be considered a small setback Monday. The Denver Nuggets, meanwhile, might be at an early tipping point after they lost on the same night.
 Both teams fell at home -- the Celtics to Orlando and the Nuggets to Phoenix -- and one of them will get back on track when they meet in Denver on Wednesday night.
 Boston's 115-105 loss to the Magic ended a six-game winning streak and a stretch where it had won 11 of 12.
 There was a positive out of the defeat -- the play of rookie Chris Cenac Jr. He was pressed into service when the Celtics opted to rest center Neemias Queta and played 12 minutes, which nearly matched his total court time for the season.
 Cenac scored just four points, but both buckets came on alley-oops that ignited the home crowd. He did commit two turnovers, but coach Joe Mazzulla said the 19-year-old Cenac had an impact.
 "You can obviously feel a difference with his athleticism when he's out there, and he made some big-time plays for us," Mazzulla said. "We're trusting him more and more each day with his mentality."
 Celtics leading scorer Jayson Tatum (26.5 points per game) praised Cenac's play in the loss, saying he "stepped up on defense," but also added that the rookie will not be treated with kid gloves.
 "We're not going to hold his hand," Tatum said. "When we get out there, we expect him to make plays because we know what he's capable of."
 Cenac's role against Denver may be limited as Queta is expected to return, but guarding Nuggets star center Nikola Jokic might take every available big.
 Jokic is coming off one of his better games, with 28 points, 15 rebounds and seven assists, but it was wasted in a 117-105 loss to Phoenix. Jokic accounted for nearly half of Denver's boards, and the undersized Suns outrebounded the Nuggets 51-35.
 The Nuggets have lost three of their last four home games and are 2-3 overall at Ball Arena, and an early recurring theme is a lack of rebounding and long-range shooting. Denver is averaging 30.9 shots from 3-point range, which ranks second-to-last in the league, but their 34.5% accuracy from deep ranks in the middle of the pack.
 The Nuggets were 1-for-9 from distance in Monday night's first half and finished 9-for-30, and also turned it over 18 times.
 "I think it's OK to lose, but (not when) someone outrebounds you and you have so many turnovers or so many mistakes," Jokic said. "... I think you can lose the game if you create open looks or you miss or it's not your night or whatever. But losing the game because you didn't finish the job rebounding or were lazy with the passes, that kills you a little bit, kills the momentum."
 In recent seasons, depth has been a problem for Denver, but coach David Adelman goes nine deep on some nights. Eight players are averaging 18 or more minutes, led by Jokic's 36.6 average. The three-time MVP is nearly averaging another triple double with 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds and 8.9 assists.
 --Field Level Media
